title: Design solution-shape — the non-frozen shape artifact and its co-reviewed split — plan 001
epic_title: Implement solution-shape v1 — the non-frozen shape artifact, co-reviewed split, and docgate gate

tasks.title: The solution-shape document class, home, and parser
tasks.goal: A solution-shape is a first-class document with its own configured home outside the design corpus, parsing to a typed value with a paired-design slug, a status, and a concrete body.
tasks.current: No solution-shape document type exists. The config surface carries `tech_designs` and `plans` roots but no shapes root, and `docs/tech-design/` is the only design-adjacent corpus a document may live in.
tasks.desired: A new closed config key roots the solution-shape corpus at a directory distinct from — and never nested under — the technical-design corpus. A shape parses to a typed value with a closed header (its paired design's slug and a status drawn from a closed set whose members are `authoritative` and `superseded-by-code`) and a concrete body carrying the schema and interfaces. Pairing resolves by slug. A malformed header, an unknown status, or a shape whose paired design is absent each yields a typed defect naming file, reason, and remedy.
scope: the new closed config key, its default, and its unknown-key rejection
the shape document parse: closed header, the status enum, and the concrete body
pairing resolution by slug between a design and its shape
typed defects for a malformed shape, an unknown status, and an unpaired shape
out_of_scope: any gate check that runs over designs or shapes (T3, T4, T5, T6)
acceptance: a well-formed shape parses to its typed value with slug, status, and body populated
a shape with an unknown status yields the named defect and no value
a shape whose paired design is absent yields the named defect
the shapes root resolves to a directory outside the technical-design corpus
key_interfaces: `config.Config` — a new solution-shapes path field, its `paths.*` parse case, and its default
a shape parser producing the typed shape value (header, status enum, body)
`schema.Defect` — the typed defect the parser emits

tasks.title: The combined review: present a design and its shape together
tasks.goal: Reviewing a technical design that has a paired solution-shape presents both the design's decisions and the shape's concrete content in one operator conversation.
tasks.current: A design and its shape are separate source files, so a reviewer needs a defined combined-review order and exact source references.
tasks.desired: When a design has a paired shape (resolved by slug from T1), the operator conversation presents both source files together — the decisions and the concrete schema and interfaces visible in one review. The presentation identifies exact tracked paths, so the reviewed bytes are the bytes that will freeze. A design with no paired shape is reviewed alone.
scope: resolve a design's paired shape before human review
present the design and shape together with exact source paths
preserve the ordinary review path for a design without a shape
out_of_scope: the gate checks (T3, T4, T5) and the lifecycle (T6)
acceptance: a design-and-shape pair is presented together with both decisions and concrete shape visible
a design with no paired shape follows the ordinary single-document review path
the presentation identifies the exact two tracked source files and their reviewed bytes
key_interfaces: the conversation presenter — where a design is joined with its paired shape for human review
the T1 pairing resolution — the only linkage between the two files

tasks.title: The gate: a frozen design carries no concrete shape
tasks.goal: The gate fails a technical design that carries concrete solution-shape content and passes one that only references its shape.
tasks.current: The gate lints design headers and structure but nothing forbids concrete schema or interface content from living inside a design body, so a design can freeze carrying volatile shape.
tasks.desired: A new check emits a `design-carries-shape` defect when a design body carries concrete schema or interface content that belongs to a shape; a design that only references its shape passes. Every technical design already merged passes unchanged. The defect names file, reason, and remedy.
scope: detect concrete-shape content inside a design body
emit the `design-carries-shape` typed defect and wire the check into the gate run
leave every existing frozen design passing
acceptance: a design carrying concrete shape yields `design-carries-shape` with file, reason, and remedy
a design that only references its shape passes clean
every existing frozen design still passes the gate unchanged
key_interfaces: a new gate check returning `[]schema.Defect`, enumerated in the `Gate` run
`techdesigns.Design` — the parsed design body the check inspects

tasks.title: The gate: witness, trace, and shape-completeness
tasks.goal: The gate flags a design invariant with no witnessing shape element, a shape element that traces to no decision, and a stateful design approved with no shape.
tasks.current: Nothing cross-checks a design's binding markup against its shape, so an invariant can lack any concrete witness and a stateful design can be approved with no shape at all.
tasks.desired: An `unwitnessed-invariant` defect fires when a design `DINV-n` has no witnessing element in its shape; an `untraced-shape-element` defect fires when a shape element cites no decision in its design; a `shape-incomplete` defect fires when a design that creates state or an interface has no paired shape. A pure-decision design that creates no state passes with no shape.
scope: the witness check across a design's invariants and its shape
the trace check from each shape element back to a decision
the shape-incomplete check for a stateful design lacking a shape
wire the three checks into the gate run
out_of_scope: the design-carries-shape check (T3), index exclusion (T5), lifecycle (T6)
acceptance: a design invariant with no witnessing shape element yields `unwitnessed-invariant`
a shape element citing no decision yields `untraced-shape-element`
a stateful design with no paired shape yields `shape-incomplete`
a pure-decision design with no state passes with no shape
key_interfaces: three new gate checks returning `[]schema.Defect`, enumerated in the `Gate` run
`techdesigns.Design` — the invariant and decision anchors the checks read
the T1 shape value — the witness/trace counterpart
tasks.overlap_accepted: shares the gate enumeration with T3, T5, T6; each adds an independent check function, no shared body

tasks.title: The index excludes the solution-shape
tasks.goal: The technical-design index never contains a solution-shape, and a shape admitted to the design corpus is a defect.
tasks.current: The index is generated from designs under the technical-design corpus; nothing asserts that shapes stay out of it or that a shape file cannot sit in the design corpus.
tasks.desired: Index generation ignores the shapes root entirely. A solution-shape found in the generated design index — or a shape document placed under the technical-design corpus — yields a `shape-indexed-as-design` defect. The index still computes design liveness exactly as before (existing entries byte-unchanged).
scope: keep index generation blind to the shapes root
the `shape-indexed-as-design` defect for a shape reaching the design corpus or index
preserve every existing design's index entry byte-for-byte
out_of_scope: lifecycle transitions (T6) and the other checks (T3, T4)
acceptance: a solution-shape never appears in the generated technical-design index
a shape document under the design corpus yields `shape-indexed-as-design`
existing designs' index entries are byte-identical before and after
key_interfaces: `techdesigns.GenIndexBytes` and `IndexEntry` — the generation the shape stays out of
the `Gate` run — where the shape-reaching-corpus defect is enumerated
tasks.overlap_accepted: shares the gate enumeration with T3, T4, T6; independent check function, no shared body

tasks.title: The shape lifecycle: authoritative, superseded-by-code, and the change branch
tasks.goal: A shape's status flips from authoritative to superseded-by-code, a stale authoritative shape is flagged, a shape-confined change leaves the frozen design untouched, and a change to a design's binding markup is refused as a shape change.
tasks.current: T1 gives a status field but no transition rule, no stale detection, and no way to tell a shape-confined change from a change that alters the paired design's binding markup.
tasks.desired: The status flips authoritative → superseded-by-code as an explicit authoring act recorded in the shape header (the interim signal until an automatic code-exists signal is designed). A `stale-shape` defect fires when an `authoritative` shape's implementing code already exists. A change confined to shape content is legal on the non-frozen shape and edits no design; a change that would alter the paired design's binding markup is refused as a shape change and routed to the design's supersession path.
scope: the status transition over the closed enum, recorded in the shape header
the `stale-shape` defect for an authoritative shape whose code exists
the discrimination between a shape-confined change and a binding-markup change
wire the lifecycle check into the gate run
out_of_scope: an automatic code-exists signal (deferred — design Q2)
acceptance: a shape flips to superseded-by-code via the explicit authoring act
an authoritative shape whose implementing code exists yields `stale-shape`
a shape-confined change leaves the paired frozen design untouched
a change altering a design's binding markup is refused as a shape change
key_interfaces: the T1 shape value — the status enum this task transitions
a lifecycle gate check returning `[]schema.Defect`, enumerated in the `Gate` run
`techdesigns.Design` — the binding markup a change is tested against
tasks.overlap_accepted: shares the gate enumeration with T3, T4, T5; independent check function, no shared body

deferred.reason: The code-diverges-from-approved-shape detector is a separate code↔shape comparison capability; the shape retires on code (FR-5, T6) regardless. Plan when a shape-vs-code diff surface is built.
